test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In what way did fiscal discipline reforms affect center-state financial relations post-1991?

options.text: States had to adhere to fiscal targets
Increased state autonomy in tax policy

solution:
The correct answer is __**States had to adhere to fiscal targets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Post-1991 fiscal reforms, states were mandated to adhere to **fiscal deficit reduction targets** to qualify for central funds and grants.
 
• The introduction of the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act** encouraged states to adopt disciplined fiscal practices.
 
• States were required to implement measures such as **limiting borrowings**, improving tax collection efficiency, and reducing non-productive expenditures.
 
• The central government provided incentives for states achieving fiscal targets, such as **debt relief packages** and additional financial assistance.
 
• Such reforms aimed at strengthening macroeconomic stability and ensuring better utilization of resources at both the central and state levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act**

 
 
• The FRBM Act was enacted in 2003 to ensure fiscal discipline and reduce fiscal deficits.
 
• It set targets for reducing the fiscal deficit and revenue deficit as a percentage of GDP.
 
• States were encouraged to adopt their own FRBM legislation in alignment with the central framework.
 
 
 
• **Debt Relief Measures for States**
 
 
• Post-reforms, states achieving fiscal targets were provided with debt restructuring and relief packages by the central government.
 
• These measures helped in reducing the financial burden on states and incentivized fiscal discipline.
 
 
 
• **Macro-Fiscal Stability**
 
 
• Fiscal discipline reforms contributed to improving macroeconomic stability by reducing the fiscal deficit and ensuring sustainable growth.
 
• Efficient allocation of resources between the center and states became a key priority.
 
 
 
• **Tax Sharing Post-Reforms**
 
 
• The 1991 reforms emphasized rationalizing tax structures to improve revenue collection.
 
• While states retained autonomy in certain tax domains, the central government introduced mechanisms for equitable tax sharing.
